# CLIENT BRIEF — HALA TOURS AGADIR (verbatim intent from the client; binding; do not edit)

## Core idea
Hala's current website dramatically undersells how much this company actually does. This is not merely a "camel ride company." They appear to operate an enormous catalog of excursions, activities, transfers and multi-day experiences.

The website should make Hala feel like: **the local Agadir travel desk you wish you'd discovered on day one.** Not GetYourGuide. Not Expedia. Not a giant marketplace. A real local team with a ridiculous amount of knowledge and options.

The site should communicate: **Tell us what sort of day you want. We probably know what to do.**

## Existing website
Canonical starting point: `halatoursagadir.com`. CRAWL THE FULL RELEVANT SITE. Do not merely copy the existing navigation. Extract the actual business underneath it.

Current contact baseline includes:
- HALA TOURS AGADIR
- physical presence at/around Hotel Hamilton, Boulevard Mohamed V, Agadir 80000
- halatoursagadir@gmail.com · contact@halatoursagadir.com
- current official site has shown phone +212 660 732 477 — VERIFY THE PHONE. Some third-party sources have conflicting variants.

The physical office/location is important. Customers should understand that they can actually come see Hala in Agadir.

Inventory the existing site fully (products, services, pages, pricing, tours, contact, policies, booking info, images, FAQs, languages, useful SEO URLs) and classify content: VERIFIED / PRESERVE · POSSIBLY STALE / VERIFY · DUPLICATE / CONSOLIDATE · BROKEN · TEMPLATE GARBAGE · UNCERTAIN. Preserve the business; do not preserve poor organisation or broken content. → `LEGACY_CONTENT_INVENTORY.md`.

VERIFY EVERYTHING CURRENTLY OFFERED. There may be additional legitimate content — do not accidentally omit it. Do not display stale products simply because they still exist in old HTML.

## Reputation / human element
Research current rating/review footprint. Reviews have repeatedly mentioned people such as Ayoub and Mustafa, and themes such as helpful advice, organisation, honest recommendations, pricing, transport, Paradise Valley, Essaouira, camel, quad. Do NOT invent roles. If a real human team story can be firmly established, use it. This should feel like booking with people, not an anonymous marketplace.

## Creative thesis
The homepage should potentially begin with something conceptually like: **What kind of day do you want?** Let visitors browse by mood/intent (e.g. Adventure · Nature · Coast · Culture · Animals · Relax · Half Day · Full Day · Go Further — not necessarily those labels; design something better if possible). The key idea is **discovery instead of a giant wall of cards.**

## Website structure (potentially)
Home · Experiences · Day Trips · Activities · Multi-Day Adventures · Transfers · Visit Hala · About / Team if verified · Reviews · Contact. Use better architecture if research suggests it.

## Experience pages
Excellent pages using current verified information. Where known include: duration · departure · pickup · itinerary · destination · food · inclusions · exclusions · languages · child suitability · recommended items · price · booking CTA.
DO NOT SHOW OLD PRICES. If current pricing is not confidently verified, "Check today's price" or "Ask us on WhatsApp" is completely acceptable.

## Physical office
Make "Visit Hala" genuinely useful. Include verified: location · Hotel Hamilton context · opening hours · directions · phone · WhatsApp · map. This may be an important conversion advantage compared with online-only marketplaces.

## Visual direction
This site should feel like Agadir opening outward into dozens of possible days. Energetic. Photographic. Joyful. Organised. Think excellent editorial travel guide + real local booking desk. Do NOT make every activity an identical white card. Find a more imaginative browsing system. The company has breadth — make breadth feel exciting rather than overwhelming.

## Cross-site test
Hala must feel like **a local world of experiences** — clearly different from Hôtel Lynx (practical urban hospitality) and Line Up Surf House (rhythm of surfing), and from the sibling Peashoot tour sites agadir-trip / agadir-camel-horse.

## Owner embarrassment test
Would Hala's owner say "We don't sell this anymore"? Fix anything uncertain.
